title: Ratio: sharing $48 in 2:3
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can read 2:3 as 2 parts and 3 parts of the same whole.
The class can find one part first by dividing the whole by the total number of parts.

modelAnswers.question: Find one part when $48 is shared in the ratio 2:3, and show the step.
Work out both shares when $48 is shared in the ratio 2:3, showing the one-part step.

commonErrors.misconception: A ratio of 3:2 means 3/2 of the whole.
commonErrors.example: A learner answers $72 for the 3-part share of $48 on the worksheet, treating 3 parts as 3/2 of the whole.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: count the parts in the whole bar, then say what fraction of the whole 3 parts really is.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: the whole is 5 parts, so 3 parts is 3/5 of $48, and one part is $9.60, so 3 parts is $28.80.

commonErrors.misconception: A ratio of 3:2 means 3/2 of the whole.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends $72 by saying 3 parts out of 2 must be 3/2 of the whole.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: name the whole in parts - add 2 and 3 first - then check whether a share can be bigger than the whole $48.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: the whole is 5 parts, not 2, so 3 parts is 3/5 of the whole and the share is $28.80, never $72.

nextSteps: Reteach counting parts out of the whole in parts with the whole bar before any further sharing questions.
Practise the add, divide, multiply sequence until finding one part first is automatic.
